- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 75% of prior peak or 10% below.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67); apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.50” values, model tends to ignore downward momentum; apply 2–4% downward adjustment for next 3–7 days.
